hypothesis: If the 103/105 state cannot be repaired by changing its three conflict-involved rows, changing four rows while retaining three mutually compatible rows may yield a scope-111 DTS.
rationale: The exact three-row completion against fixed rows 1, 3, 5, and 6 found only 84 compatible rows and no disjoint triple. The next smallest structural repair class changes one additional row. Fixing rows 1, 3, and 5 leaves 66 unused difference slots, exactly enough for four new 15-difference Golomb rulers with six gaps, making this an exact finite packing problem rather than a stochastic proxy search.
expected_information_gain: A disjoint quadruple gives a directly validator-checkable target DTS. A complete no-quadruple result closes this specific four-row repair basin; a timeout remains capability evidence only and does not establish global infeasibility.
method: Compile research_tools/search_dts_four_row_completion.cpp with WSL2 g++ -O3. Fix rows 1, 3, and 5 of the exact memetic 103 state. Recursively enumerate all normalized six-mark rows with scope<=111 whose 15 differences avoid the fixed 45-difference mask and are internally unique. Build an inverted difference index and perform exact recursive four-row set packing with rare currently available differences and at most six gap branches. Emit generation and packing completion status, and independently validate any assembled seven-row result with research_tools/verify_dts.py and research_tools/verify_dts_independent.py.
metric: Fixed-row difference count, compatible-row catalog size, generation/packing nodes and timeout flags, maximum packed depth, gap count, and independent validator result
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A complete seven-row assignment accepted by both independent integer verifiers is exactly the frozen true objective. Finite catalog depth or timeout is methodological evidence only.

configuration.enumeration: exact recursive compatible-row generation plus rare-difference exact packing

kill_condition: Stop at the first complete disjoint quadruple and preserve it for independent validation, at the 180-second deadline, or after complete generation and packing. Do not infer global DTS infeasibility from this fixed-three decomposition or from timeout.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if the assembled rows pass both independent verifiers

previous_best_comparison.three_row_completion: zero disjoint triple against fixed rows 1, 3, 5, 6
previous_best_comparison.full_row_completion: zero compatible row against fixed rows 1 through 6
previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: four-row decomposition changes one additional row while retaining three good rows

interpretation: Complete compatible-row generation against fixed rows 1, 3, and 5 produced 9,644 rows from 35,649 generation nodes. Exhaustive rare-difference four-row packing visited 180,037 nodes without timeout, reached no disjoint quadruple, and produced no target.
what_was_learned: The 103/105 memetic state cannot be completed by changing rows 0, 2, 4, and 6 while preserving rows 1, 3, and 5. This closes the tested four-row repair basin exactly and does not imply global DTS infeasibility.
recommended_next_action: Close this memetic-repair line. Any further DTS work should use a genuinely different global construction or a materially stronger exact-search capability rather than adding repair depth here.
repetition_justification: This is not a repeat of the previous three-row completion: it fixes a different three-row subset, changes four rows instead of three, and performs a new exact compatible-row enumeration and packing search.
